paper.title: Risk-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Mobile Manipulation

review.question: 2025-07-19 至 2026-07-19 的 loco-manipulation 研究在哪些控制、学习、数据、感知、评测和部署方向取得了可验证进展，其适用边界与未解问题是什么？

relevance.reason: Mobile-manipulation study of risk-sensitive navigation and reaching under egocentric depth uncertainty.

sections_read.purpose: Identify tail-risk failures in cluttered mobile manipulation.
Inspect distributional teacher learning and depth-policy distillation.
Verify risk behavior and task competence.

research_question: Can risk sensitivity learned with privileged state be distilled into a depth-only mobile-manipulation policy?
contributions: A two-stage distributional-RL teacher and DAgger student with runtime-adjustable risk conditioning.

method.summary: A privileged distributional critic learns a risk-conditioned teacher; DAgger distills its actions into an egocentric depth policy.
assumptions: Training simulation exposes representative aleatoric uncertainty.
Depth sensing and privileged teacher state can be aligned during distillation.

study_context.sample_or_scale: Simulation-only experiments across risk settings and clutter configurations.

evaluation.design: Risk-aware and risk-neutral teachers/students are compared on returns, task metrics and qualitative trajectories.

findings.finding: Risk-conditioned behavior transferred to a depth-only student without a reported collapse in overall task competence.
findings.scope: The simulated environments and modeled aleatoric uncertainty.

author_stated.limitation: The work is simulation-only, models aleatoric rather than epistemic uncertainty, uses shaped rewards, and relies on imitation for the student.

reader_inferred.boundary: Runtime risk control is not yet validated under real sensing, dynamics or novel hazards.
reader_inferred.basis: All experiments are simulated and the paper explicitly defers hardware validation.

transfer_boundary: Evidence supports risk-aware simulation policies, not deployable safety guarantees.

design_strengths: Separates privileged risk learning from visuomotor deployment.
Evaluates a continuum of runtime risk attitudes.
design_risks: Simulation and reward design define the risk distribution.
critical_appraisal.baseline_fairness: Risk-aware and neutral policies share the task and policy family.
critical_appraisal.metric_validity: Distributional returns reflect the optimized notion of risk but may not cover unmodeled hazards.
critical_appraisal.reproducibility: Method and training phases are described.

evidence_cards.claim: The study reports a depth-only mobile-manipulation policy whose risk sensitivity can be adjusted at runtime while retaining task performance comparable to risk-neutral methods in simulation.
evidence_cards.relation: Supports explicit risk conditioning as an emerging control axis, subject to hardware validation.
evidence_cards.summary: The conclusion summarizes risk-aware student competence and transfer through imitation learning.
evidence_cards.source_context: Our approach trains risk-aware visuomotor policies for mobile manipulation conditioned on egocentric depth observations with runtime-adjustable risk sensitivity, achieving comparable performance to risk-neutral methods, and we show learnt risk-aware behaviours can be successfully transferred through Imitation Learning.

verification.rationale: The conclusion directly states the observation modality, runtime adjustment, comparison and transfer mechanism.
